requirements.title: DT editing invokes user-provided formatting instead of default derived-type formatting
requirements.definition: DT specifies that a user-provided procedure is used instead of processor default input/output formatting for a derived-type effective item.

pending.DT-user-provided-procedure: Deferred to clause 12/15 defined-I/O ownership: define a type whose formatted DT output writes exactly 'D'; internal WRITE(buf,'(DT)') value must then expect 'D'.

requirements.title: DT literal and v values are passed as iotype and v_list arguments
requirements.definition: A DT character literal contributes to iotype as DT concatenated with the literal, and v values are passed as the v_list array argument.

pending.DT-literal-iotype: Future defined-I/O fixture: DT'X' must pass iotype exactly 'DTX' to the procedure, which can write 'X' so internal WRITE expects 'X'.
pending.DT-v-list-values: Future defined-I/O fixture: DT(1,-2) must pass v_list values [1,-2]; the procedure can write 'V' only after verifying the list, so internal WRITE expects 'V'.

requirements.title: DT requires an accessible corresponding defined-I/O interface and a derived-type item
requirements.definition: A derived-type variable or value corresponding to DT requires an accessible corresponding defined input/output procedure; DT shall not correspond to a non-derived-type effective item.

pending.accessible-defined-io-interface: Future positive control defines an accessible formatted DT I/O interface that writes exactly 'D'; internal WRITE(buf,'(DT)') value expects 'D'.
pending.DT-derived-type-item: Same future control uses a derived-type scalar effective item and expects exactly 'D'.
pending.DT-nonderived-item-invalid: Negative source shape: WRITE(buf,'(DT)') 7; repair by using a derived-type value with an accessible DT procedure. Only the effective-item derived-type property differs.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, two rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_138.json. The reviewer re-derived the receipt (21 sections, 64 units, 0 hash mismatches) and INDEPENDENTLY RE-PARTITIONED the four crowded pages - p303, p304, p306 and p307 - unit by unit, confirming among other things that 13.8.8 genuinely owns only p1 despite covering six rounding-mode descriptors. A mis-attributed paragraph would have been invisible in the totals, since 64 would still be 64. The zero-numbered-R/C claim was verified: R1323 appears on p302 but belongs to the sibling 13.7.2.4 packet. FOUR blocking findings, all closed. C138SR-001: a negative was filed against 13.7.5.2.2, which only CROSS-REFERS to the rule - the actual prohibition is 13.7.5.1 p1 'On input, w shall not be zero' - and 'Note that w cannot be zero' is a reminder, not a prohibition; the facet is now an explicit dependency. C138SR-002: four units filed LATITUDE AS REQUIREMENTS - the fifth occurrence of the mixed obligation/latitude class, and notably the MIRROR of the sibling packet, which filed obligations as permission; all four were split into requirement and permission subunits. C138SR-003: an output-control facet sat under 13.9 p1, which owns only the input prohibition; output moved to p2. C138SR-004: a negative named a descriptor but NO DATUM, so nothing showed the p6 branch was reached; it now uses datum zero with (G4.1E3), where s=1 reaches the F branch, n=e+2=5 and w-n=-1, with repair (G7.1E3) expecting exactly '0.     ' - the reviewer derived all of that independently. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977.
